title: Gupta Science and Mathematics

cards.b: The Gupta age is called classical because of science as much as art. Prelims asks who wrote what: Aryabhata, Varahamihira, Brahmagupta, Sushruta, Charaka. Many were from this or the slightly later period.

Aryabhata (b. 476 CE, Kusumapura; Aryabhatiya, 499 CE) gave the value of pi as 3.1416, explained eclipses by shadows, said the earth rotates on its axis and used place value including zero. Sine tables, solution of linear equations (kuttaka). India’s first satellite (1975) was named after him.

Court of Chandragupta II or later; Brihat Samhita (weather, architecture, gems), Pancha Siddhantika (five astronomical schools), Brihat Jataka (astrology). He noted that the moon shines by reflected light of the sun.

Brahmagupta (Brahmasphutasiddhanta, 628 CE; Ujjain) treated zero as a number with rules, negative numbers, gravity as attraction. Later Bhaskara II (Lilavati, 12th century). Zero and decimal system spread via Arabs (Al-Khwarizmi), known as “Arabic numerals”. The Bakhshali manuscript (Pakistan) has a dot for zero (radiocarbon dated by Oxford in 2017 to 3rd or 4th century).

Sushruta Samhita: surgery, rhinoplasty, 100+ instruments. Charaka Samhita: internal medicine, three doshas, attributed to Charaka at Kanishka’s court. Vagbhata’s Ashtanga Hridaya (c. 7th century). Nagarjuna (the alchemist) wrote on metals. Hospitals existed; Fa-Hien saw free charitable dispensaries at Pataliputra.

The Mehrauli Iron Pillar (Delhi, 4th century, inscription of Chandra, likely Chandragupta II) has resisted rust for 1,600 years because of high phosphorus content and a protective film. A giant copper Buddha was found at Sultanganj (Bihar). Wootz steel developed in the south. Gupta gold coins show excellent minting.

Historians like R. S. Sharma argue the “golden age” label hides rural decline and the rise of land grants. Scientific progress came from a small elite and sometimes borrowed Greek ideas (e.g. Romaka Siddhanta, Yavanajataka). Yet the numerals and zero were original.

ISRO’s Aryabhata satellite (1975) and Bhaskara satellites; Indian Knowledge Systems (IKS) Division at the Ministry of Education; Ayush Ministry promotes Ayurveda; Sushruta is honoured as the “father of surgery” in India. The national space day is on 23 August (Chandrayaan-3 landing, 2023).
